answer_raw:
**Medellín** offers the greatest stretch for your money, followed by Florianópolis, with Lisbon being the most expensive option.

**Medellín**
The money stretches furthest here; while specific monthly totals for Medellín aren't provided, coastal Colombian rentals for studios range from **$320 to $960** (as of June 2026) [1]. In similar Colombian cities, one-bedroom units in modest neighborhoods average **$213 to $256** (as of June 2026) [1]. With a $4,000 budget, you would live very comfortably here.

**Florianópolis**
A single person can live on roughly **$1,500** per month (as of June 2026) [2]. Rent for a one-bedroom in a good area typically runs between **R$2,500 and R$3,800** (as of 2026) [3], which converts to roughly **$659–$1,025** (as of June 2026 based on the R$5.1 per US$1 rate) [4]. You could live well on a $4,000 budget, but it is significantly more expensive than Colombia [4].

**Lisbon**
This is the most expensive of the three; living in Lisbon requires roughly **€4,800** to maintain a certain standard of living, whereas the same lifestyle in Florianópolis would cost roughly **€2,856** (undated) [5]. A $4,000 budget would be much tighter here than in the other two cities.

| City | Relative Cost | Rent (1-BR/Studio) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Medellín** | Lowest | **$213–$960** (as of June 2026) [1] |
| **Florianópolis** | Moderate | **$659–$1,025** (as of June 2026) [2][4] |
| **Lisbon** | Highest | Significantly higher than **€2,856** (undated) [5] |
